subject: How to interpret standardized coefficients for latent variable in CFA?

messages.author: 6667ef04b386b9ec
messages.subject: How to interpret standardized coefficients for latent variable in CFA?
parts:
Hello there!

I am fitting a CFA model with the following syntax:

    cfa_esp <- ' Tarefa =~ Coop. + Esf.Melh. + PapelImp. 
                 Ego =~ Pun.Erros + Recon.Desig. + Riv.Membr.'
    m0_cfa <- cfa(cfa_esp, data =data, orthogonal = F, estimator = "WLSMV")

And I obtain these results from the coefficients:

    summary(m0_cfa, standardized = T)$PE

    Latent Variables:
                             Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
      Tarefa =~                                                                   
        Coop.                   1.000                               0.688    0.891
        Esf.Melh.               0.639    0.042   15.170    0.000    0.439    0.793
        PapelImp.               0.677    0.043   15.678    0.000    0.466    0.797
      Ego =~                                                                      
        Pun.Erros               1.000                               0.262    0.403
        Recon.Desig.            4.872    1.514    3.218    0.001    1.277    1.388
        Riv.Membr.              1.069    0.221    4.834    0.000    0.280    0.307


How can I interpret `Std.all` column?

This is my try for each estimate column:

+ A unit increase in `Tarefa` implies in .639 units increase in `Esf.Melh.`;
+ One standard deviation increase in `Tarefa` implies in .439 units increase in `Esf.Melh.`
+ The correlation of `PapelImp.` and `Tarefa` is .797 (since we are building latent variable, Std.all is interpreted as correlation);

This is what I thought it was right. However, the Std.all coefficient is 1.388 for `Ego` and `Recon.Desig.`. So, how can I interpret these coefficients?

Thanks
Obs.: I also made this question on stats.stackexchange. Thanks

             # Correlação
             Tarefa ~~ Ego
           '
But I don't think that this makes difference in the interpretation.

Best Regards

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: How to interpret standardized coefficients for latent variable in CFA?
parts:
A standardized loading over 1 is an impermissible solution, but judging the large standard error on the unstandardized coefficient it may not be significantly over 1.

That said, the standardized loadings on Ego are widely disparate, especially with only three items. You may have an empirical underidentification issue. I would go back and examine the (polychoric?) correlation matrix, as well as the residual correlation matrix from the CFA.

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: How to interpret standardized coefficients for latent variable in CFA?
parts:
Look into "Heywood case" where a residual variance is negative. You haven't said explicitly, but you very likely have a negative residual variance for Recon.Desig. You should look into your data and results to see how concerned to be.

Also, you're dealing with factor loadings, which are a kind of regression coefficient, but usually aren't discussed in the same language. I'm also not sure why you changed from regression language in your first two points to correlation language in your third, which is incorrect.

Pat
